description:
## Goal

Give every logical source one stable semantic owner and each submitted text an immutable version, then make explicit replacement transfer the complete current publication atomically. A plain new submit_code remains a distinct contribution, never an implicit edit keyed by a filename or insertion order.

## Evidence

CodeSubmission carries only name and text. CodeMap::define and SourceMap::add_code are append-only and mint a fresh CodeId for every call. Reusing a CodeId would make retained spans render against different bytes, violating immutable diagnostic provenance. Minting a fresh CodeId preserves provenance but currently creates a second publisher with no operation that withdraws or transfers the prior source complete output frontier.

This missing boundary is shared by fz-kdt.24 global-function ownership, fz-kdt.30 named-module ownership, fz-tfn.53 type-declaration ownership, fz-kdt.32 requester expectations, fz-tfn.40 diagnostic/content separation, fz-tfn.45 generated callable identity, and fz-tfn.20 source reclamation. A type-only replacement API or separate owner registry would duplicate authority and leave other outputs incoherent.

## Required contract

- Stable source identity is a typed semantic key, distinct from display names and immutable CodeId or SourceId versions.
- submit_code creates a new source owner. replace_source names the exact existing owner and creates a fresh immutable source version.
- Replacement publishes or rejects one complete source delta across functions, modules, structs, macros, types, expectations, diagnostics, scheduler claims, reads, waits and retained products. Consumers never observe a mixed old/new source.
- Equal reproduction preserves authoritative values, allocations and generations and wakes nobody. Relevant changes move only exact transitive dependents. Unrelated roots do no work.
- Old versions remain only while exact diagnostic/artifact owners retain them and become reclaimable by fz-tfn.20; no age, order, filename or canonical-string authority.
- A failed replacement preserves the entire accepted prior version and provenance. A new conflicting owner receives the owning domain diagnostic without mutating the first owner.

## Strategy

Use the semantic Output Contract Loop. Pin the smallest two-source/new-owner/replacement examples at the public API, trace every source-owned publication boundary, and choose the minimal immutable owner/version model from the data model upward. Define the all-output transaction before exposing replacement. Fold concordant owner registries and delete append-only compatibility paths, whole-source scanners, rollback mirrors, and temporary migration adapters at cutover.

Do not expose a partial replacement API, infer identity from CodeSubmission.name, overwrite SourceMap bytes, or install per-domain replacement authorities.

## Acceptance

- Distinct source submission and explicit replacement are separate typed operations.
- Same-text replacement performs essentially no compiler work and preserves allocations/generations/artifacts.
- Unrelated edits do not invalidate a requested root; relevant edits recompute only exact transitive dependents.
- Function, module, struct, macro, type, expectation and generated-callable ownership moves atomically, including Blocked then failed runs.
- Diagnostics name the exact immutable source version; retained old artifacts keep valid provenance; superseded versions become exactly reclaimable.
- Deterministic causal telemetry proves evaluations, movements, generations, allocations, compile counts and byte-identical artifacts.
- Current ownership/replacement tickets are reconciled without parallel stores or duplicated semantics; docs describe one source lifecycle.
- TDD, ticket-scoped cold adversarial review, full applicable gates, one commit and close. Any temporary scaffolding has a removal ticket and is removed by the final cutover.

## Ordering decision still required

Decide whether this is the shared prerequisite for fz-kdt.24, fz-kdt.30, fz-tfn.53 and fz-kdt.32, or whether those owner registries land first and this ticket composes them. Do not wire dependencies until the atomic split is proven. The duplicate-type rule in fz-tfn.53 also still requires explicit confirmation.
title: Define one atomic source-replacement ownership boundary
